source_notes: repo https://github.com/godotengine/godot; merged PR or fixed issue

facts.claim: Godot issue #73936 exists, is closed, was opened 2023-02-25, and reports .new() on custom Object classes about 76x slower in 4.0 RC5 than 3.5.1 (about 15 ms vs 1,147 ms for 10,000 instances)
Issue #73936 was closed as completed by PR #81037 (merged 2023-08-28 as commit 75bc686)
PR #81037 is a GDScript member-init / constructor-path speedup
PR #81037 is titled 'Ensure OpenXR classes are declared properly' and its review discusses OpenXR class declarations and doc files, not the instantiation path
The instantiation fix is a single mistake in plain-Object allocation in engine core, described as a bug that caused major unexpected behaviour differences, shipped in 4.1.2
The 4.1.2 release notes do not mention GDScript for this fix
Repository licence is MIT (LICENSE text is the MIT permission notice; copyright 2014-present Godot Engine contributors and 2007-2014 Juan Linietsky, Ariel Manzur)
The pre-fix 4.0-era commit hash named in the seed is pinned
Offline smoke build of the trimmed GDScript headless recipe is green

full_card.band: 8 h tier. Frontier agent likely finds allocation hotspots and gets partial speedup; the fix itself is one lever, so the top of the band is not a multi-lever scope.
full_card.build_cost: 3 (2-5 days): full Godot scons build plus trimming recipe; smoke build unverified.
full_card.deliverable: Patch to the module sources speeding up script instance creation (new, _init, member init, constructor path) with unchanged semantics.
full_card.gates_anticheat: Hidden semantics tests with side effects; benchmark on unseen classes. Caching instances is blocked by side-effect tests. Editing tests or build config is not closed by the seed.
full_card.grading_surface: GDScript test subset in repo plus hidden scripts compared on output, and a hidden instantiation benchmark (wall-clock median). Moderate surface, about tens to low hundreds of cases.
full_card.local_fit: C++ build of Godot on 8 cores / 16 GB is heavy but plausibly fits; gVisor has no kernel feature needs.
full_card.lookup: partial. Public fix in 4.1.2 and git history; a frontier model may recall the Godot allocation code in outline. History-less snapshot required.
full_card.provenance: Issue #73936 (closed, MIT repo, reported on 4.0 RC3/RC5). Closing PR #81037 is public and shipped in 4.1.2; its title and scope are OpenXR declarations, with the allocation fix described only in release notes as a small mistake in plain-object allocation.
full_card.reference: Upstream fix commits, but the closing PR is a small allocation fix in core. A reference of 150+ non-blank lines in the GDScript VM is not supported by the evidence.
full_card.ships: Trimmed headless Godot recipe at a pre-fix commit (hash not pinned in seed). Smoke build not run (empty). Build is a full scons C++ build, so the cost is not verified offline.

v1.kill_reason: One-lever scope: the closing upstream fix (PR #81037, 4.1.2) is a single allocation mistake in core Object creation, not a GDScript VM member-init or constructor-path change. The reference cannot reach the 150-line, multi-lever bar that the seed's framing requires, and the seed's own reference is not substantial.

Band.why: 8 h band is plausible for partial speedup, but no dated public evidence of agent performance; band cannot reach 4 or 5.

Build.why: Full Godot build plus trimming is estimated at 2-5 days; smoke build not run.

Fit.why: C++ build is heavy but within 8 CPU / 16 GB in principle; not verified.

Hor.why: A full build and iterative benchmarking exist, but the lever is narrow, so sustained work is limited.

Multi.why: Essentially one lever (instance allocation and init); partial-credit buckets are weak.

Nov.why: Public neighbours are 0.12 and 0.09 and not crowded; sibling seeds are not public tasks.

Real.why: Real MIT Godot issue #73936 with closing PR #81037 and a 4.1.2 release.

Ref.why: The public closing fix is a small allocation change, far below the 150-line reference bar, and its scope differs from the seed's VM framing.

Seal.why: The fix is public in 4.1.2 and in history, and a frontier model may recall it in outline; a snapshot is needed but reconstruction is likely.

Surf.why: Hidden benchmark plus GDScript subset gives moderate surface; not thousands of cases.

spike_plan.kill_if: The pre-fix/fixed ratio is under 1.5x, or the trimmed build cannot be produced offline within 90 minutes, or the fix turns out to be a single line with no GDScript-side lever.
spike_plan.pass_if: The pre-fix build is at least 3x slower than the 4.1.2 build on the 10k-instance benchmark, the test subset is identical on both, and the trimmed build finishes in under 90 minutes.
steps: In a throwaway Linux container with network, clone godot at the 4.0-era parent of the 4.1.2-era allocation fix (locate the pre-fix commit by bisecting the PR #81037 range, since the seed gives no hash).

Build headless template_release with only the gdscript module kept (scons platform=linuxbsd target=template_release, module_*_enabled=no for non-essential modules); run in background and record wall time.
Build the same tag with the closing fix applied (4.1.2 tag) as the upstream comparison.
Write a 10,000-instance benchmark of a custom Object subclass with .new(), a typed-member variant and an inheritance-depth-3 variant; run each 5 times and take the median.
Check determinism: the median spread across 5 runs and the test subset pass/fail on both builds.

v1.summary: Issue #73936 and its closing PR #81037 are real and MIT-licensed, but PR #81037 is a small OpenXR-titled change whose allocation fix is a single core mistake, not a GDScript instantiation rewrite. The seed's scope is a one-lever, narrow optimization with a weak reference and an unverified build, so it is killed as K10 unless the scope is widened to a multi-lever set.
